T-M3-06 was infeasible as written (hidden prerequisite). It asked for a minimal new-product, mode: consumer fixture inside test_validate_unattended_readiness.py to report status == 'ready'. validate_unattended_readiness also calls product_intent.validate_scope. With a task_route profile, 'ready' needs the full product contract: task_goal, task_scope, frozen intents, requirement_refs, a confirmed plan and, after M2, a confirmed experience-direction intent. Every existing fixture in that file is profile-less for this reason. Fix: split into two tests. (1) A profile-less graph in the Must #9 shape with both loops, asserting blockers == []. (2) The same graph plus a product-route consumer profile, asserting blocker codes only and not status. Test (2) asserts no experience-gate or M1 codes with both loops declared, experience_gate_without_repair_loop after dropping the runtime loop, and missing_experience_gate after removing the runtime critique node. The acceptance selects both node ids. The plan, the M3 design U7 bullet, its touch-list row and M3.json were all updated.

T-M3-01 acceptance counted tests by a name prefix the plan never stated. The command counts names starting 'test_validate_app_experience_pipeline_' and requires at least 3, but the plan only said 'three cases'. The game test file it mirrors has just two tests. The three exact test names are now in the plan.

T-M5-10 evidence check strengthened. It already verified case ids, verdicts, the single Read tool call and the fixture and response sha256 values, but responses.md could be any text and under_test/notes could be empty. It now requires a '## E<n>' section for each of the nine cases in responses.md and non-empty under_test, notes and resolved_model per case. The heading convention follows the existing product-review-thought-tests. I dry-ran the python one-liner against synthetic evidence in the scratchpad and it exited 0.

T-M5-11 failure loop strengthened. A loop could be recorded as 'closed' with empty fixed_files/pinned and no retest transcript. It now requires a '## E<n>b' section in responses.md for every first-round failure, and non-empty fixed_files[] and pinned[] when the loop is closed. Its write set includes the product-review and cross-exam twins, bootstrap-planning.md, suppress-rules.md and the Codex parity script, but its acceptance only ran a subset of their guards. I added the twin diff-count == 12 check, test_experience_lens_parity.py, test_codex_contract_checks.py, 'validate_app_experience_pipeline.py .' and the M1 same-line invariant grep. The check passes on synthetic evidence.
residual_risks: The new cross-module depends_on entries use foreign task ids (T-M1-07, T-M2-10, T-M3-10, T-M4-07, T-M4-08, T-M6-03/04/05). This departs from the stage-1.2 rule 'depends_on intra-module only'. It was the only way to express module-completion ordering, because the frozen registry has no interface implemented by the sink tasks and M6 exposes none. build_task_dag.py resolves depends_on over the combined task list: ok=true, 0 errors, no cycle. If the M1/M2/M4 reverse critic renumbers a sink task, these entries must be updated. They are valid only when all six task files are fed to the DAG builder together.

The M1/M2/M4 task files (outside my scope) have the same race class. One example is T-M1-01's acceptance running test_product_intent_session.py while T-M2-01 edits it. The cross-module pass should check these.

T-M5-14 deliberately runs the full claude/meta-skill unit suite, about 6 minutes and 8-10 minutes in total. Frozen R-M5-05 requires this, and the command compares the failure set to the four baseline ids rather than exit 0. If the supervisor's acceptance rerun has a timeout shorter than about 10 minutes, this task will fail spuriously.

T-M5-10 and T-M5-11 evidence is recorded by the executor itself. The acceptance now checks real content: case ids, verdicts, one section per case, sha256 binding of the criteria and the responses. It cannot prove the subagents were truly fresh-context or that the transcripts are unedited. That still relies on the supervisor reading the host trace.

T-M5-06 and T-M5-07 cannot be verified before M1-M3 land. The risk is whether the good workflow passes all of M1, M2 and M3 plus mobile-UI coverage, repair-loop declaration, plan confirmation and validate_scope, and whether force_past_front_door leaves plan confirmation consistent. The design addresses each pre-existing gate, and the acceptance runs the real tests, so an infeasible fixture surfaces as a blocked task rather than a false pass.

T-M3-04 intentionally makes a game creative-quality-critique.json with non-empty gates.must_fix_before_release fail check_artifacts. No test or fixture in the repo has that shape today, confirmed by grep. Generated game projects will see the stricter behaviour on upgrade.

T-M5-16 is a reality gate. Its runbook is present, the anchor resolves and no task depends on it. Its step 3 has a human retrieve the original ink-scent request text from session history.
